chunks: Sa'd narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hakam ibn Miskin, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I enter the mosque and the Imam has already bowed, so I bow with his bowing while I am alone, and I prostrate. When I raise my head, what should I do?' He said: 'Stand and go to them; if they are standing, stand with them, and if they are sitting, sit with them.'
ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they join the congregational prayer after the Imam has already bowed and prostrated alone?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration clarifies the procedural nuance for a latecomer who joins the congregation after the Imam has already completed the bowing and prostration individually. It establishes the principle of *muqaddam* (precedence) in joining the group, ensuring the individual aligns their final standing or sitting with the congregation's current state, thereby preserving the unity of the prayer (*jama'ah*). This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on communal cohesion and the practical adaptability of ritual acts within the framework of following the Imam.
